#### [com.wix.media.site_media.v1.FilesService.BulkDeleteFiles](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/bulk-delete-files) # Package: mediaManager # Namespace: files # Method: Bulk Delete Files # Method link: https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/bulk-delete-files # Method API Endpoint: POST https://www.wixapis.com/site-media/v1/bulk/files/delete ## Method Code Examples ### Available request examples - Bulk delete files - HTTP request example > These are the request examples found in this result. Read the full method article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/bulk-delete-files and locate an example by its exact title to get it complete. --- Code Example: Bulk delete files --- ### Bulk delete files ```javascript curl -X POST \ 'https://www.wixapis.com/site-media/v1/bulk/files/delete' \ -H 'Authorization: ' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{ "fileIds": ["4acbb8_7596aeebcf5c41eca01c0d99667ac967.mp3", "3vcbb7_7446aeebcf5c41eca01c0d99665bc866.mp3"] }' ``` --- Method Response Shape --- ## Method Response Shape ```json {} ``` --- Method Description --- ## Method Description: Deletes the specified files from the Media Manager.
The deleted files are moved to the Media Manager's trash bin (`TRASH-ROOT` folder) unless permanently deleted. To permanently delete files, specify the `permanent` parameter with the value `true`. Permanently deleting files isn't reversible, so make sure that these files aren't being used in a site or in any other way as the files will no longer be accessible. Note the following: * The specified files can be from different folders. * Moving multiple files at once is an asynchronous action, and may take time for the changes to appear in the Media Manager. * Attempting to delete files that are already in the trash bin doesn't result in an error. * If a site contains deleted media files, the deleted media files still appear on the site as the files are still in the Media Manager (in the trash bin). * You can use Bulk Restore Files From Trash Bin to restore files from the Media Manager's trash bin. ## Method Permissions: MEDIA.SITE_MEDIA_FILES_MOVE_TO_TRASH ## Method Permissions Scopes: Manage Media Manager: SCOPE.DC-MEDIA.MANAGE-MEDIAMANAGER ## Additional Method Code Examples --- Code Example: HTTP request example --- ... example body omitted under the current line budget — listed under "Available request examples"; read the full doc with its exact title for the complete example ... > Next: read the full method article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/bulk-delete-files using the suitable read tool to get the complete code examples and method description. > If you need more detail about the request or response shape, read the full method schema using the suitable tool. --- #### [com.wixpress.exposure.progallery.ProGallery.BulkDeleteGalleryItems](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/pro-gallery/bulk-delete-gallery-items) # Package: proGallery # Namespace: undefined # Method: Bulk Delete Gallery Items # Method link: https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/pro-gallery/bulk-delete-gallery-items # Method API Endpoint: POST https://www.wixapis.com/progallery/v2/galleries/{galleryId}/items/delete ## Method Code Examples ### Available request examples - Delete multiple gallery items > These are the request examples found in this result. Read the full method article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/pro-gallery/bulk-delete-gallery-items and locate an example by its exact title to get it complete. --- Code Example: Delete multiple gallery items --- ### Delete multiple gallery items ```javascript curl -X POST \ 'https://www.wixapis.com/progallery/v2/galleries/432c362d-1440-4205-b9cb-35ea11a22682/items/delete' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: ' \ -d '{ "itemIds": [ "fa499c86-aee9-11ea-8c85-12879e2400f0", "cb499c86-aee9-11ea-8c85-12879e2400f0" ], }' ``` --- Method Response Shape --- ## Method Response Shape ```json { "itemIds": [ "string" ] } ``` --- Method Description --- ## Method Description: Deletes multiple media items from a gallery. ## Method Permissions: PRO_GALLERY.MANAGE ## Method Permissions Scopes: Manage Galleries: SCOPE.DC-PROGALLERY.MANAGE-GALLERIES ## Method Schema Summary: The `bulkDeleteGalleryItems` method allows for the deletion of multiple media items from a gallery. It is a POST request to the URL `https://www.wixapis.com/progallery/v2/galleries/{galleryId}/items/delete`. The method requires one parameter: * `itemIds`: An array of strings, where each string is a GUID representing the ID of a media item to be deleted. This parameter is required and must contain between 1 and 1000 item IDs. The response, `BulkDeleteGalleryItemsResponse`, includes an `itemIds` field which is an array of strings containing the IDs of the media items that were successfully deleted. --- **Questions and Answers:** 1. **Q: How do I delete multiple media items from a gallery?** A: Use the `bulkDeleteGalleryItems` method with an array of item IDs. 2. **Q: What is the maximum number of items that can be deleted in a single request?** A: You can delete up to 1000 items in a single request. 3. **Q: What format should the item IDs be in?** A: Item IDs must be in GUID format. 4. **Q: Is it possible to delete zero items using this method?** A: No, the `itemIds` parameter requires at least one item ID. 5. **Q: What information is returned after deleting items?** A: The response returns the IDs of the media items that were successfully deleted. > Next: read the full method article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/pro-gallery/bulk-delete-gallery-items using the suitable read tool to get the complete code examples and method description. > If you need more detail about the request or response shape, read the full method schema using the suitable tool. --- #### [business-management/google-business-profile/media-upload-v1/sample-flows](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile/media-upload-v1/sample-flows) ## Resource: Sample Flows ## Article: Sample Flows ## Article Link: https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile/media-upload-v1/sample-flows ## Article Content: # Media Upload API: Sample Flows This article presents possible use cases and corresponding sample flows that you can support. It provides a useful starting point as you plan your implementation. > **Prerequisite:** every flow assumes the site already has a Google connection, established through > the Google Business Profile Connection API, and that the location is already imported. Changes are > queued per location, identified by Google's location ID. ## Save a full gallery The site owner has arranged a gallery of photos and hits save. Google accepts only about 10 edits per minute per profile, so apply the whole set through the queue instead of one immediate write per photo. 1. Collect the changes. Each addition needs a publicly reachable `sourceUrl`, a `category` such as `LOGO`, `COVER`, or `INTERIOR`, and `format: "PHOTO"`. 2. Call **Bulk Create Media Uploads** with up to 52 changes and `operation: "CREATE"` on each. The call returns in well under a second without calling Google. One call has to be either all additions or all removals, so send two calls if the save mixes both. 3. Inspect `results[].itemMetadata.error`. The call reports per-item failures instead of aborting, so a `200` does not mean every change was queued. ... 87 more lines ... > Next: read the full article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/google-business-profile/media-upload-v1/sample-flows using the suitable read tool. --- #### Read the full method article at https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/folders/bulk-delete-folders and locate an example by its exact title to get it complete. --- Code Example: Bulk delete folders --- ### Bulk delete folders ```javascript curl -X POST \ 'https://www.wixapis.com/site-media/v1/bulk/folders/delete' \ -H 'Authorization: ' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{ "folderIds": ["25284aa06584441ea94338fdcfbaba12", "9v38fdcfbaba12eeb55bcf5c41eca01c0"] }' ``` --- Method Response Shape --- ## Method Response Shape ```json {} ``` --- Method Description --- ## Method Description: Temporarily deletes the specified folders from the Media Manager.
The deleted folders are moved to the Media Manager's `trash-root` folder (trash bin) unless permanently deleted. To permanently delete folders, specify the `permanent` parameter with the value `true`. Permanently deleting folders isn't reversible, so make sure that the files in these folders aren't being used in a site or in any other way as the files will no longer be accessible. Note the following: * When a folder is deleted, the files in that folder are deleted. * The specified folders can be from different parent folders. * Moving multiple folders at once is an asynchronous action, and may take time for the changes to appear in the Media Manager. * Attempting to delete folders that are already in the trash bin doesn't result in an error. * If a site contains files from a deleted media folder, the files still appear on the site as the deleted folder is still in the Media Manager (in the trash bin). * You can also use the [Bulk Restore Folders From Trash Bin](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/assets/media/media-manager/folders/bulk-restore-folders-from-trash-bin) method to restore folders from the Media Manager's trash bin. ## Method Permissions: MEDIA.SITE_MEDIA_FOLDERS_MOVE_TO_TRASH ## Method Permissions Scopes: Manage Media Manager: SCOPE.DC-MEDIA.MANAGE-MEDIAMANAGER ## Additional Method Code Examples --- Code Example: HTTP request example --- ... example body omitted under the current line budget — listed under "Available request examples";
